host.lead: Turn this computer into your own mail server. Your other devices connect to it directly — nothing goes through the cloud.
host.story: It works over Tailscale, a private tunnel between your own devices. Nothing is opened to the internet.

host.autostart: Start ohmail when you log in
host.autostartWhy: So your mail is reachable without opening the app first — while this computer is awake.
host.autostartUnknown: The system wouldn't say whether this is on. Flipping the switch sets it fresh either way.

host.offHint: Your other devices stop reaching this computer until you turn it back on.

host.guideNoCli: Tailscale isn't on this computer yet. It's a free app — install it and sign in, then come back here.
host.guideNotRunning: Tailscale is installed but not running. Open the Tailscale app, then check again.
host.guideNotLoggedIn: Tailscale is running but signed out. Sign in in the Tailscale app, then check again.
host.guideNoDnsName: Tailscale hasn't named this computer yet. Turn on MagicDNS in the Tailscale admin console, then check again.
host.guideServeRefused: Tailscale wouldn't publish this computer to your devices — serving may be switched off for your tailnet. Check the Tailscale admin console, then try again.
host.guideLocalDoorRequired: Serving works when ohmail opens your own mailbox on this computer. It stays off while this install mirrors a hosted account.
host.guideEngineNotServing: The mail engine on this computer isn't running yet, so there is nothing to serve. Give it a moment, then check again.
host.guideListenerPending: Nearly there — the engine is opening its door for your devices.
host.guideListenerSkipped: The engine didn't open its door this launch. Turning this off and on again starts it clean.
host.guideListenerFailed: The engine couldn't open its door — most often the port is already taken. Turn this off and on again, or pick another port under Advanced.
host.guideConfigInvalid: The saved settings didn't make sense, so nothing is served. Turn this off and on again to start clean.
host.guideGeneric: It's on, and something is in the way. Turning it off and on again usually clears it.
host.lanOptionWhy: Serves your mail to the ohmail app on your own network — no Tailscale needed for that. The connection is secured with a key this computer keeps, and the pairing code carries it, so the app knows it is really talking to this computer. A phone browser can't use it: a browser has no way to check that key.
host.lanPickWhy: The address of this computer on your network. Devices on the same network use it to reach the mail API.
host.lanNone: No usable network address was found on this computer.
host.lanListFailed: This computer's network addresses couldn't be read. Check again in a moment.
host.lanAloneWhy: You can still turn on same-network access: the ohmail app on your own network reaches your mail at this computer's address, secured by a key this computer keeps. Not for phone browsers — a browser needs the Tailscale address above.
host.lanServing: The mail API is served at {address} — for apps on your network, while this computer is awake. If a device can't reach it, check that this computer's firewall allows port {port}.
host.lanBlocked: The mail API is running at {address}, but this computer's firewall is not letting anything through to port {port} — no device on your network can reach it yet.
host.lanBlockedFix: Open the port, then check again. This command needs an administrator password:
host.lanFailed: The same-network door couldn't open — most often the port is already taken. Turn this off and on again, or pick another port under Advanced.
host.lanInvalid: The saved network address isn't usable anymore — this computer's address may have changed. Turn this off and on again and pick a current one.
host.lanBrowserNote: A phone browser can't use this address — it is secured with a key only the ohmail app can check, and a browser would warn instead. Browsers use the Tailscale address instead.
host.lanAddHint: You get a one-time pairing link to copy into an app or API client on your network. It works once and expires in five minutes.
host.lanMintedLead: Copy this pairing link into the app or API client on the other device. It pairs over your network in one step.
host.keyWhy: A device pairing over your network shows these characters before it pairs. If it shows different ones, something else is answering for this computer.

autoUnsub.title: Unsubscribe when I screen out or mark spam
autoUnsub.on: Screening a sender out also sends their unsubscribe, where they offer one-click and the sender was confirmed by your mail provider, or by the signature the sender's own domain put on the message.
autoUnsub.off: Their mail is filed and nothing is sent.
autoUnsub.microcopy: One request per list, once, from our servers — so your address and reading times stay out of the sender's log. Senders who offer no one-click link are filed and nothing is sent for them, and a request already sent cannot be taken back.
autoUnsub.microcopyComputer: One request per list, once, from your computer — so the sender sees its network address. Senders who offer no one-click link are filed and nothing is sent for them, and a request already sent cannot be taken back.

about.p1: A demo mailbox, invented for it — nobody real, nothing real. Every key and every click works, and none of it leaves this tab: there is no network here at all.
about.p2: The Screener holds first-time senders until you decide. One click files a sender to Ohbox, News or Receipts — the ✓ half also marks the held mail read — and the decision becomes a rule for future mail. News and Receipts share a reading stream where an item turns read once it rests on screen; a quick scroll past leaves it unread. Tags group messages across views without moving them.
about.accountHeaderMissing: This server does not name the account it answers for, so this window cannot tell an answer meant for you from one meant for somebody else who was signed in on this browser a moment ago. Everything else still applies; this is the one check it cannot make. Ask whoever runs it to update.

ai.title: AI proposes. You decide.
ai.body: Rules run first and do the bulk of the work with no AI at all — the design goal is that most of your mail is filed deterministically, by rules you can read and change. Where judgment actually helps, ohmail offers something: a door for a new sender, a draft in your voice, a nudge for a thread that went quiet. Every one of them waits for your yes, and nothing ever sends itself.
ai.status: The AI features run against a live model in production: the Screener proposes a door for a waiting sender, with a confidence and a reason, and the composer writes a first draft when you ask it for one. Both are proposals — they wait for your yes, nothing files or sends itself, and a pattern only begins running on its own once you have confirmed it often enough to graduate into a rule. The metering and spend limits that govern managed AI are in place and enforced: when the budget runs out the rules carry on, and nothing else changes.

compare.aiOthers: Built into their cloud — or missing entirely

data.title: Where your mail lives.
data.sub: Three ways to run one product. The mailbox is the master in all of them; what differs is whose machine holds the working copy.
data.desktopRuns: Your machine. No account, no ohmail server in the loop — macOS, Windows and Linux.
data.desktopCopy: On your own disk, so it reads and searches with no network. It never leaves your machine.
data.desktopAi: Optional: your own key, or a local model.
data.selfRuns: A server you run — the same open server behind ohmail.app, from one compose file.
data.selfCopy: In a database on your box, where it powers search and sync to your devices.

data.cloudRuns: Our EU servers — the same server, run for you, and awake when your devices are not.
data.cloudCopy: On servers in Switzerland, encrypted at rest, up to your plan's storage; as your plan's storage fills, the bodies of your oldest messages are emptied to make room for new mail, and fetched back from your mail server when there is room again; the messages stay findable, because their headers, preview and the words search finds them by are kept. Deleted from the live database with your account.
data.cloudAi: Included in your plan and metered. When the credits run out, mail keeps flowing rules-only.
data.same: Cloud is self-hosting, done for you: the same open server, the same organizer, the same mailbox as the master. What changes is whose machine holds the copy — and that we bill for running it.

data.aiNote: AI on Cloud goes to Anthropic under commercial API terms: your mail is never used to train models, and requests are retained only briefly (currently up to 30 days); there is no zero-retention agreement yet.

faq.title: Questions, answered.
faq.q1: What happens to my existing folders?
faq.a1: Nothing destructive. The folders you already have are left exactly as they are; ohmail organizes new mail into real IMAP folders on your server. Everything stays visible to any other mail client, on any device.
faq.a2: Anytime. Your mail never needs exporting — the originals live on your own server, in ordinary folders ohmail created in place, and nothing we do touches them. Be clear about what Cloud holds, though: a full copy of that mail — bodies, headers, subjects and senders — alongside your rules, tags and notes, because that is what makes search and push work. All of it is deleted from the live database with your account.
faq.a3: On Cloud: via the Claude API (Anthropic), under commercial API terms and within your plan's credits — the model runs at Anthropic, not on our servers. On the desktop app: wherever you point it — your own API key, or a local model through Ollama so nothing leaves your machine — set in the app, and off until you configure it. On a server you run: the model its operator configures — a hosted one under their own key, or one they run themselves — and without one everything else works. Either way, rules with no AI at all run first and are meant to handle most mail — and you can switch the AI off entirely without losing a single feature that files your mail.
faq.a4: The unit your plan is measured in. Actions cost what they cost us: screening a new sender or filing a message is 1 credit, a drafted reply 15. Drafting reads a whole thread and writes prose, so it costs more than sorting one message — pricing them the same would only mean charging everybody for the expensive one. When the monthly budget runs out, mail keeps flowing rules-only until the next cycle. There are no overage charges — ever.
faq.a5: Not as a matter of practice, and our admin tools do not display message content — every response the console can produce is checked by a test that writes a marker into every text column of every table and fails if any of it reaches a staff response. The database refuses them too: the console reads through a column-restricted database role that cannot select message content, and it verifies that restriction before it reads anything. The honest fine print: Cloud mail is stored unencrypted at the application level and is not end-to-end encrypted, so someone with production database access could technically read it; that access is held by very few people, and the product privacy policy will spell out who and under what conditions when it publishes. On Desktop the question doesn't arise — your mail never reaches our servers at all: the app runs as a real mail client against your own server, on macOS, Windows and Linux alike. Separately, nobody else gets to watch you read either: a spy pixel is blocked by default — loading them is a choice you would have to make in Settings — and one disguised as an ordinary picture loads like any picture each time the message's pictures are fetched, before it is blocked. On Cloud, ordinary pictures load through our own proxy, so the sender's server sees us and never your address; the desktop app and the standalone phone app fetch pictures themselves, so there the sender sees that device's address.
faq.a6: Any IMAP mailbox: your own domain at Metanet or Infomaniak, iCloud, Gmail, Outlook, a self-hosted server. If it speaks IMAP, ohmail organizes it in place. Native Exchange sync over Microsoft Graph is on the roadmap; Microsoft 365 connects over IMAP, like every other mailbox here.
faq.q7: Is there a trial for Cloud?
faq.a7: Yes — 14 days, no card. It is the whole product: rules, sync, push and the web app all run, and it comes with 500 credits so the drafts and the Screener's suggestions are yours to try. Spend those and mail keeps flowing rules-only; the monthly allowance begins when a subscription does. Desktop needs no trial at all; it is free.
faq.q8: Desktop or Cloud — what’s the real difference?
faq.a8: The same model, the same vocabulary, and deliberately not the same privacy posture — that is the honest difference. Desktop is free and fully standalone: all processing local, no account, no artificial limits. It is a real mail client on all three platforms — it connects to your own IMAP server and organizes your mailbox on your machine, and because your mail is on your own disk it is there to read with the network down. Its AI, if you want one, is your own API key or a local model through Ollama — set in the app, off until you configure it. Cloud adds the web app, push notifications, always-on processing while your computer sleeps, and AI included from $9 a month — and it holds a copy of your mail on our servers to do that. The same download does either one; which door you take is a choice inside the app. Both are open today.

account.eraseRefusedSubCancelled: Your account was not deleted. Your subscription was cancelled before the error; nothing else was removed. Start the confirmation again to delete the account.

account.mail: Your mail is on your own server, in the ohmail folders it is filed into. This deletes our copy; your mailbox stays exactly as organized as it is now.
account.gone2: Every mailbox you connected, and the stored credentials for it.
account.gone3: Every message, thread, contact and note we mirrored, with your rules, screener decisions and workflows.

account.goneWhen: One database transaction, immediately, and the copy in this browser is wiped too.
account.kept1: One billing row with a random id and no name, plus the credit ledger, the subscription record and the link to Stripe. Your address on it is overwritten. Financial records carry a retention obligation that Art. 17(3)(b) preserves. The record of what our staff looked at or changed on the account stays too, under the same id. Hashes of your sign-in tokens stay for up to 400 days after they expire, so an app still signed in is told the account is gone.
account.keptSelfHost: An account row with a random id and no name, and hashes of its sign-in tokens for up to 400 days after they expire, so an app that still holds one is told the account is gone.
account.keptSub: Your subscription is cancelled immediately as part of this. The days already paid for are not refunded.
account.backups: Backups expire on their own schedule.

providerPicker.otherSub: another provider or your own server
providerPicker.protonNote: Proton Mail reaches other mail apps only through Proton Bridge, an app that runs on your own computer. Connect a Proton mailbox from the ohmail desktop app on the computer where Bridge runs; “{other}” here does not reach it.
providerPicker.protonNoteDesktop: Proton Mail reaches other mail apps only through Proton Bridge. Start Bridge on this computer, choose “{other}”, and type 127.0.0.1 with port 1143 for incoming mail and 1025 for outgoing mail, with the password Bridge shows, not your Proton password. ohmail then asks you to trust Bridge's own certificate.
providerPicker.need_gmail: an App Password from your Google account, with 2-Step Verification on.
providerPicker.need_microsoft: an app password, or Sign in with Microsoft where it is offered.

providerPicker.need_webde: IMAP switched on in WEB.DE's settings, and your WEB.DE password.
providerPicker.need_tonline: the e-mail password from the Telekom E-Mail Center, not your Telekom login.
providerPicker.need_bluewin: your full bluewin address and the mailbox's own password.
providerPicker.need_imap: your provider's incoming (IMAP) and outgoing (SMTP) server names, and the mailbox's password.

providerPicker.note_gmail: Gmail signs in only with an App Password, not your Google password. Turn on 2-Step Verification first, or the App Passwords page says it is not available. Give the App Password any name, then paste its 16 letters here, with or without the spaces. Some work, school and Advanced Protection accounts, and accounts that sign in with security keys only, cannot create App Passwords; ohmail cannot connect those yet: ask your administrator to allow App Passwords, or connect another address.
providerPicker.note_microsoft: ohmail connects to Microsoft over IMAP, like every other mailbox — native Exchange sync over Microsoft Graph is on the roadmap and is not shipped. When this deployment has a Microsoft application registration, you can sign in with Microsoft instead and no password is stored; that option is offered only where it is actually configured. Otherwise you need an app password, which requires security defaults to be off on the account; on some work tenants an administrator has disabled IMAP entirely, and then it cannot connect at all.
providerPicker.note_icloud: iCloud needs an app-specific password (Apple ID → Sign-In and Security). Your username is usually the full @icloud.com address, even if you sign in to Apple with a different one.
providerPicker.note_yahoo: Yahoo requires an app password generated under Account Security. The account password will not work for IMAP.
providerPicker.note_fastmail: Create an app password in Settings → Privacy & Security → Integrations, scoped to “Mail (IMAP/SMTP)”. Fastmail lets you revoke it on its own later.
providerPicker.note_gmx: GMX ships with IMAP switched OFF. Turn it on first in Settings → POP3 & IMAP, then use your ordinary GMX password here.
providerPicker.note_infomaniak: Use your mailbox address and its password. If the account has two-factor authentication, create an application password in the Infomaniak Manager first.
providerPicker.note_webde: WEB.DE ships with IMAP switched off. Turn it on first under Einstellungen → POP3/IMAP Abruf, then use your ordinary WEB.DE password here. If the account has two-factor authentication, create an application-specific password for it instead.
providerPicker.note_tonline: Telekom Mail signs mail apps in with its own e-mail password, not your Telekom login password. Set one in the Telekom E-Mail Center first, then use it here with your full t-online.de address.
providerPicker.note_bluewin: Use your full bluewin address and its e-mail password, the password of the mailbox itself.
providerPicker.note_imap: A provider not listed here, or your own server. You need the IMAP host, the SMTP host, and a password for the mailbox; your provider's help pages call these “incoming” and “outgoing” servers. If your domain's mail is hosted by Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, choose Gmail or Microsoft instead.

mailboxes.standDown_organized_elsewhere_unknown: Another ohmail organizer has claimed this mailbox. This install reads it — mail arrives, search works, nothing is filed from here.

mailboxes.standDownHowServer: It will not start again on its own. “Take over on this server…” below checks who holds the mailbox and then offers to move the organizing here; the other install reads it from that point.
mailboxes.standDownHowLapsed: It will not start again on its own. “Take over on Cloud…” below checks the mailbox and then offers to organize it here.
mailboxes.standDownHowLapsedServer: It will not start again on its own. “Take over on this server…” below checks the mailbox and then offers to organize it here.

mailboxes.organizerEffectLapsedServer: Taking over: this server starts organizing this mailbox on its next pass and removes any claim a stopped install left behind.
mailboxes.organizerQueued: Cloud will start organizing this mailbox on its next pass.
mailboxes.organizerQueuedServer: This server will start organizing this mailbox on its next pass.

mailboxes.desktopRemovedNotCleared: This mailbox could not be cleared from this computer yet, so it has not been removed. Nothing was deleted from the mailbox itself. Remove it again to retry.
mailboxes.desktopStateSignInRefused: The mail server refused the sign-in.

mailboxes.desktopOrganizeHere_removed: That mailbox was removed from this machine. Add it again in the Desktop settings pane instead.
mailboxes.desktopOrganizeHere_no_mailbox: This machine has no mailbox for that address.

mailboxes.desktopNoBrowser: This computer would not open a browser. The page is at ohmail.app.
mailboxes.desktopManageOnServer: Mailboxes are managed on your server's web app
mailboxes.desktopManageOnServerWhy: Connecting a mailbox or changing its password stores a mailbox password; removing one deletes the password stored for it. mailboxes.desktopNoBrowserServer: This computer would not open a browser. The page is at {host}.
mailboxes.desktopHoldsCount: This computer holds {count, number} of your account's {total, number} messages. The rest stay on your account and load when you reach them in a list or open one — nothing is missing.
mailboxes.desktopCopyIsACopy: Your mail lives on your mail server. What this app keeps on this computer is a copy — you can remove it and nothing is lost from the mailbox itself.
mailboxes.removeStopsReader: This computer stops reading this mailbox. It was not organizing it, so nothing else changes there.
mailboxes.removeMailSafe: Your mail is untouched. The ohmail folders and every message stay on your mail server — removing a mailbox here deletes nothing from it.
mailboxes.removeCredential: The password ohmail stored for this mailbox is deleted.
mailboxes.removeCalendarConnection: The calendar connection that uses this Apple ID stays. You can remove it in Calendar settings.
mailboxes.removeCalendarPossible: If you use this Apple ID in Calendar, that connection stays. You can remove it in Calendar settings.
mailboxes.removeScheduled: Scheduled sends from this mailbox are closed rather than sent. Each goes back to Drafts saying why.
mailboxes.removeCopyStays: The mail ohmail has already copied stays in your account and stops being updated. Deleting your account removes it.
mailboxes.removeCopyLocal: This computer's copy of this mailbox's mail is deleted. Your mail server keeps every message.

mailboxes.removeReconnect: You can connect this mailbox again later.

mailboxes.removeKeepChoice: Remove, and keep ohmail's copy of its mail
mailboxes.removeEraseChoice: Remove, and erase ohmail's copy of this mailbox's mail
mailboxes.removeEraseWhat: Your mail stays on your own mail server, which keeps the master copy. Only ohmail's copy goes, and that cannot be undone.
mailboxes.removeCopyErased: ohmail's copy of this mailbox's mail is erased from your account: its messages, its drafts and its folder list. Your mail server keeps every message.
mailboxes.removeEraseTypeLabel: To erase, type this mailbox's address
mailboxes.removeEraseMismatch: That is not this mailbox's address, so nothing was removed or erased. Type it exactly as it appears above.
mailboxes.removeErased: {address} is removed, and ohmail's copy of its mail is erased: {messages, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}} and {drafts, plural, one {# draft} other {# drafts}}. Your mail server still has every message.
mailboxes.removeErasedUnanchored: {address} is removed, and ohmail's copy of its mail is erased: {messages, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}} and {drafts, plural, one {# draft} other {# drafts}}. mailboxes.factorBodyErase: Erasing ohmail's copy of a mailbox's mail cannot be undone, so your account asks for a fresh second factor first.
mailboxes.listBehind: The change is saved. The mailbox list has not been read since, so it stays hidden until it is.
mailboxes.erasingLeft: Erasing ohmail's copy — {count, plural, =0 {finishing} one {# message left} other {# messages left}}

mailboxes.organizeHereWhatLegacy: This asks for the mailbox; it does not take it. Quit and reopen ohmail and this computer starts organizing it. Its copy of your mail is left alone either way.
mailboxes.organizeHereWhatNobody: Nothing organizes this mailbox right now. Confirm, and this computer starts on its next pass — within a minute — and from then on it moves mail into your folders, screens strangers and applies your rules.
mailboxes.organizeHereCountermandWhat: This cancels the stop you asked for. This computer keeps organizing the mailbox and nothing hands it over.

mailboxes.organizeHereQueuedLegacy: Asked for. Quit and reopen ohmail to organize this mailbox from this computer. Until then this one stays stood down.

mailboxes.stateOrganizingServer: This server files this mailbox, whether or not this page is open: it moves mail into your folders, screens strangers and applies your rules.

mailboxes.stopOrganizingWhatCloud: ohmail Cloud stops filing this mailbox and goes on reading it. Your folders and everything in them stay where they are. Any install can take it over afterwards, ohmail Cloud included.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingWhatServer: This server stops filing this mailbox and goes on reading it. Your folders and everything in them stay where they are. Any install can take it over afterwards, this server included.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingQueued: Asked for. This computer stops organizing on its next pass — within a minute.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingQueuedCloud: Asked for. ohmail Cloud stops organizing on its next pass — within a minute.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingQueuedServer: Asked for. This server stops organizing on its next pass — within a minute.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingSiblingLapse: Another copy of this computer keeps organizing this mailbox until its claim lapses.

mailboxes.stopOrganizingSiblingLapseServer: Another copy of this server keeps organizing this mailbox until its claim lapses.

mailboxes.stopOrganizingNotServer: This server was not organizing this mailbox.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingHandBack: Hand the mailbox back — the mail stays where it is.

mailboxes.stateClaimLeftBehind: Cloud is not organizing this mailbox, but its claim is still on it. Nothing else will take the mailbox over while the claim is there.
mailboxes.stateClaimLeftBehindServer: This server is not organizing this mailbox, but its claim is still on it. Nothing else will take the mailbox over while the claim is there.

mailboxes.releaseClaimWhat: This takes Cloud's claim off the mailbox and changes nothing else. Your folders and everything in them stay where they are, the password is kept, and any install can take the mailbox over afterwards, including this one.
mailboxes.releaseClaimWhatServer: This takes this server's claim off the mailbox and changes nothing else. Your folders and everything in them stay where they are, the password is kept, and any install can take the mailbox over afterwards, this server included.
mailboxes.setupAgainWhy: Walks through what ohmail files, how far back it screens, and AI — with what is set now filled in. Nothing moves until you agree.
mailboxes.desktopAddWhy: This computer can open more than one. Setup asks for the server and the password, tests them, and asks how far back to screen — nothing moves until you agree.
mailboxes.removeLastDoor: This is the only mailbox on this computer, so ohmail returns to its setup screen afterwards.

mailboxes.desktopManageOnHostWhy: Connecting a mailbox or changing its password happens in ohmail on {host}. This computer shows what {host} holds.
mailboxes.desktopHoldsCountHost: This computer holds {count} of the {total} messages {host} holds for you. The rest loads from {host} when you reach it.

mailboxes.signInAgainWhy_gmail: Changed your Google password? That ends every App Password: create a new App Password and give it to ohmail here. The copy on this computer, your folders and everything ohmail has organized stay exactly where they are.

mailboxes.signInAgainAskHint: Sealed on this computer and sent only to the server above.

onboarding.welcomeTitle: Mail from people you said yes to.
onboarding.vanishedTitle: That mailbox is no longer connected

aiProvider.offDescription: Mail is filed by rules alone. Nothing is sent to a model.
aiProvider.choiceNoneWhy: Rules only. The Screener still holds first-time senders; nobody suggests, nothing drafts.
aiProvider.choiceAnthropicWhy: Sender, subject and a short extract go to api.anthropic.com, billed to your Anthropic account. A draft also sends extracts from the thread and matching knowledge-base notes.
aiProvider.choiceOpenaiWhy: Sender, subject and a short extract go to api.openai.com, billed to your OpenAI account. A draft also sends extracts from the thread and matching knowledge-base notes.
aiProvider.choiceOpenCodeGoWhy: Sender, subject and a short extract go to opencode.ai and on to the provider behind the model you choose, billed through your OpenCode account. A draft also sends extracts from the thread and matching knowledge-base notes.
aiProvider.choiceOllamaWhy: Sender, subject and a short extract go to Ollama at {host}. A draft also sends extracts from the thread and matching knowledge-base notes. Nothing leaves this computer.
aiProvider.choiceOllamaWhyElsewhere: Sender, subject and a short extract go to Ollama at {host}, which is not this computer. A draft also sends extracts from the thread and matching knowledge-base notes.
aiProvider.keyStoredPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the stored key
aiProvider.keyHint: The key goes to the mail engine on this computer, which seals it under a key in your keychain. It is never shown again and is sent only to {vendor}.
aiProvider.keyCannotStore: This install has no keychain to seal a key with, so a key cannot be stored on this computer. A model running here needs no key.
aiProvider.goKeyCannotStore: This install has no durable key, so it cannot safely store an OpenCode Go key. No plaintext fallback is used.
aiProvider.goPrivacyBilling: You manage eligibility, model privacy and billing in your OpenCode account. ohmail cannot inspect, change or enforce those settings, and does not guarantee upstream retention or training behavior. Go allowance use, account-side Extra usage/Use balance, and Auto-reload/Auto-recharge may result in charges; OpenCode controls them.
aiProvider.goFreePreviewNote: Models marked free or preview stay on offer. Their upstream data terms can differ from the paid models', and ohmail cannot check them; choose one only if that suits the mail it will read.
aiProvider.goChooseModels: The key works. Choose a model for suggestions and one for reply drafts below.
aiProvider.goConfigVerified: Go is configured for classification, screening and drafts.
aiProvider.goInferenceNotTested: Verification checked only the key and workspace model configuration; inference, quota and runtime availability were not tested.
aiProvider.verdictNoGoKeyDetail: Enter your dedicated Go key to read workspace model configuration. No inference request is sent.
aiProvider.verdictGoUntested: OpenCode Go configuration not verified yet.
aiProvider.verdictGoUntestedDetail: Verify uses only the Console config read; it does not run inference.
aiProvider.verdictGoNoModels: The workspace lists no supported OpenCode Go Chat Completions models.
aiProvider.verdictOk: {vendor} answered. {count, plural, one {1 model} other {# models}} available.
aiProvider.verdictOkDetail: Pick the models below, then save.
aiProvider.verdictUnauthorizedDetail: Check the key in your {vendor} console and paste it again.
aiProvider.verdictUnreachableOllama: Nothing answered at {host}. Is Ollama running?
aiProvider.verdictTimeout: {vendor} took too long to answer. Try again.
aiProvider.verdictModelAbsent: The model you chose cannot be used.
aiProvider.verdictModelAbsentDetail: Pick one of the {count} models below.
aiProvider.verdictNoModelsOllama: Ollama is running and has no models yet.
aiProvider.verdictNoModelsOllamaPull: Pull one in a terminal, then test again: ollama pull gemma3:12b — or ollama pull llama3.2 on a machine with less memory.
aiProvider.verdictNoModelsListed: {vendor} listed no models, so there is nothing to choose here yet.
aiProvider.verdictBadResponse: {vendor} answered with something ohmail could not read.
aiProvider.verdictRequestRejected: OpenCode Go could not verify this request. Check your OpenCode account or try again.
aiProvider.verdictCredential: A key is stored and this install's keychain does not open it. Paste it again to seal it afresh.
aiProvider.verdictInternal: Something on this side went wrong. Try again.
aiProvider.verdictNoKeyDetail: Paste a key above and test it. Nothing is sent until then.
aiProvider.verdictUntestedDetail: Nothing is offered until the test passes.
aiProvider.modelClassifyHint: Judges a first-time sender. One short call per sender.
aiProvider.modelDraftHint: Reads the thread and writes a draft. Costs more per call than a suggestion.
aiProvider.modelsWait: Test first — the list comes from {vendor}.
aiProvider.removeWhy: Removes the stored keys from this computer. Mail keeps arriving and keeps being filed.
aiProvider.note: Only what a model needs to answer is sent. A suggestion sends the sender, the subject and a short extract. A draft sends the same for the message you reply to, plus the sender and a short extract of up to 20 other messages in its thread and up to 5 matching knowledge-base notes.

desktopScreener.postureLabel: Keep my Ohbox for what matters
desktopScreener.postureWhy: On: real people, plus the service mail you act on. Obvious bulk — newsletters, promotions — goes to News and Receipts. Off: anything from a sender you have written to reaches the Ohbox. It changes how the NEXT messages are filed; mail already in your Ohbox stays where it is.
desktopScreener.impersonationWhy: When a waiting letter claims to be a company it can't be from, ohmail moves it to Spam on its own, without AI. The Screener lists each one, and you can put it back.
desktopScreener.saveFailed: That did not save. Nothing has changed.
desktopScreener.autoSuggestNoModel: This install has no model set up yet, so nothing is being suggested. Add your own API key or point ohmail at a model on this machine under Desktop, and suggestions start with the next batch of mail.
desktopScreener.autoSuggestOff: Off. Senders wait in the Screener until you press Suggest, and nothing is sent to your model before you do.
desktopScreener.autoSuggestOn: On. Each time ohmail finishes bringing in new mail, it asks your model about the new senders waiting in the Screener, so the advice is already there when you look. It still files nothing and writes no rules — every sender waits for you.
desktopScreener.autoSuggestPrivacy: Only the sender, the subject and a short extract go to the model you configured — the same request the Suggest button makes, just without you pressing it.
desktopScreener.autoSuggestGoAllowance: OpenCode Go suggestions can use your Go allowance; account-side Extra usage may incur charges.
desktopScreener.wordsWhy: Used whenever a model judges a sender for you — as your mail is filed, and when you ask about the senders waiting in your Screener. It judges them against your sentence rather than ours. With no model set up the words wait: your mail is filed by rules either way.
desktopScreener.wordsOffline: Your words live on your ohmail Cloud account, so they can’t be edited while this install is offline. Your mail keeps reading; this comes back with the connection.
desktopScreener.wordsOfflineServer: Your words live on your ohmail server, so they can’t be edited while this install is offline. Your mail keeps reading; this comes back with the connection.
desktopScreener.suggestNoModel: Suggestions come from a model you set up. There is none on this install yet.

desktopScreener.suggestGo: {count, plural, one {Suggest for 1 sender} other {Suggest for # senders}}

desktopScreener.suggestSetupAfterRefusal: {reason} Set one up in Settings, Desktop.
desktopScreener.suggestEmpty: There are no new suggestions for these senders.
desktopScreener.suggestNote: Uses the model you set up. Senders already answered for are not asked about again.

desktopDoor.localLead: This computer connects to your mail server directly. Your password is stored on this {machine}, encrypted under a key this install keeps here, and is never sent to us.
desktopDoor.localPasswordHint: For most providers this is an app password rather than the password you sign in with — the note under your provider says which.
desktopDoor.localUser: Username, if it is not the address
desktopDoor.serverAskLead: Give the address you open ohmail at in a browser. This app will check that your server is there before it asks for anything else.
desktopDoor.serverSignInLead: Signing in happens in the mail engine on this {machine} — the password and the code go straight there and are not kept anywhere else.
desktopDoor.serverAddress: Your ohmail address on that server
desktopDoor.serverCaHintBefore: If your server issues its own certificates, put its root certificate in a file named
desktopDoor.serverCaHintAfter: in this app's data folder first. ohmail verifies certificates and has no way to skip that.
desktopDoor.serverCaPathBefore: If your server issues its own certificates, save its root certificate as
desktopDoor.serverCaPathAfter: first. ohmail verifies certificates and has no way to skip that.
desktopDoor.cloudLeadSignIn: The copy of your mail on this {machine} is where you left it. Signing in happens in the mail engine on this machine — the password and the code go straight there and are not kept anywhere else.
desktopDoor.cloudLeadRevoked: This {machine} was signed out — from another device, or after a security check. The copy of your mail here was removed.
desktopDoor.cloudLeadReused: This {machine} used a sign-in that had already been renewed. If you did not restore or copy anything, change your password. The copy of your mail here was removed.
desktopDoor.cloudLeadExpired: Your sign-in on this {machine} expired after a long time without use. The copy of your mail here is where you left it.
desktopDoor.cloudLeadSealFailed: The sign-in saved on this {machine} could not be read, so it has to be made again. The copy of your mail here is where you left it.
desktopDoor.cloudUnreachableTitle: ohmail Cloud could not be reached — retrying.
desktopDoor.serverUnreachableTitle: Your ohmail server could not be reached — retrying.
desktopDoor.cloudUnreachableWhy: The mail already here keeps reading; new mail arrives once it answers.
desktopDoor.cloudSealPausedTitle: This {machine} would not save your sign-in.
desktopDoor.cloudSealPausedWhy: New mail waits until it can; you stay signed in.
desktopDoor.cloudLead: Your account is organized on our servers and this app keeps a copy. Signing in happens in the mail engine on this machine — the password and the code go straight there and are not kept anywhere else.
desktopDoor.cloudBrowserHint: Your browser opens ohmail.app. Sign in there if you are not already, then press “Open ohmail” on that page and this app comes forward signed in.
desktopDoor.cloudHandoffLabel: Or type the code the page shows
desktopDoor.cloudHandoffHint: The code works once and lasts a couple of minutes.
desktopDoor.noBrowser: This {machine} would not open a browser. The page is at ohmail.app/link-desktop.
desktopDoor.linkNoBrowser: This {machine} would not open a browser. The address is {address}.
desktopDoor.linkNotOpened: ohmail could not open this link. The address is {address}.
desktopDoor.browserSignInFailed: The browser sign-in could not be started.
desktopDoor.resetBrowserFailed: The password reset page could not be opened in your browser.
desktopDoor.cloudJoinNoBrowser: This {machine} would not open a browser. The page is at ohmail.app/join.
desktopDoor.cloudSetupOnWeb: Mailboxes are connected in ohmail on the web. Sign in here once yours is connected.
desktopDoor.cloudApproveHint: Your browser opens ohmail.app. Confirm this {machine} there — nothing to type here.
desktopDoor.cloudApproveBusy: The ohmail server is busy. Still waiting.
desktopDoor.cloudApproveUnreachable: ohmail could not be reached. Still trying.
desktopDoor.cloudApproveExpired: This request expired before it was confirmed. Start again.
desktopDoor.cloudAddressForDoor: The ohmail mailbox this {machine} will hold
desktopDoor.cloudSignInWithCode: Sign in with a code instead
desktopDoor.cloudApproveDenied: This request was declined in the browser.
desktopDoor.cloudApproveUsed: This request was already used. Start again.
desktopDoor.cloudApproveOwned: This {machine} holds the mail of a different ohmail account, so the browser cannot sign it in to this one. Type the address of the account you want: its mail then replaces the other copy on this {machine}.
desktopDoor.cloudApproveDoorChanged: This {machine} was set up another way while you were confirming, so nothing was signed in. Start again.
desktopDoor.cloudApproveNotSaved: This {machine} could not save the sign-in. Try again; if it keeps failing, quit ohmail and open it again.
desktopDoor.rendererReloaded: ohmail's window stopped and was reloaded.
desktopDoor.updateClosing: Installing the update. ohmail closes when it is done.
desktopDoor.doorNoneWhy: No mailbox has been chosen on this install yet.
desktopDoor.aboutAppWhy: The build running in this window.
desktopDoor.aboutPreviewWhy: A nightly build of the next version. It keeps its own data, apart from an installed ohmail, and the next night's build replaces it.
desktopDoor.aboutPublisherWhy: The company that writes this app.
desktopDoor.aboutLicenceWhy: Free software. The source of this app is published, and you may build it yourself.
desktopDoor.aboutDoorCloudWhy: A hosted account. The organizing happens on our servers and this app keeps a copy.
desktopDoor.aboutDoorServerWhy: A server you run does the organizing; this app keeps a copy.
desktopDoor.aboutDoorLocalWhy: This computer opens your mailbox directly. Nothing about your mail is sent to us.
desktopDoor.aboutMailNote: Your mail lives in your mailbox, on your own server. ohmail files it into folders there, where every other mail app you own can see them, and keeps a copy on this computer so the app is fast and works offline. Stop using ohmail and your mail is exactly where you left it.
desktopDoor.aboutLinksCloud: Privacy and the list of companies we rely on: ohmail.app/privacy and ohmail.app/subprocessors. Source: github.com/trafficflowhq/ohmail.
desktopDoor.diagnosticWhy: Writes one file about how this install is running: versions, counts, error codes and recent log events, never addresses, subjects or folder names. Nothing is sent.
desktopDoor.diagnosticWritten: Written to {path}. Nothing was sent. Attach it to a message to us yourself if you want us to look.
desktopDoor.diagnosticFailed: The file could not be written. Nothing was sent.
desktopDoor.mailboxWhyOrganizes: The mailbox this copy of ohmail organizes.
desktopDoor.mailboxWhyReadsNamed: The mailbox this copy of ohmail reads. {name} organizes it.
desktopDoor.mailboxWhyReads: The mailbox this copy of ohmail reads. Another ohmail organizer organizes it.
desktopDoor.mailboxWhyReadsNobody: The mailbox this copy of ohmail reads. Nothing organizes it now — Settings → Mailboxes has the button to organize it here.
desktopDoor.doorCloudWhy: A hosted ohmail account. The organizing happens on our servers and this app keeps a copy.
desktopDoor.doorLocalWhy: Your own mail server, opened by this computer. Nothing about your mail is sent to us.
desktopDoor.credCloudLiveWhy: This install holds a session for your hosted account.
desktopDoor.credCloudOutWhy: There is no session for this account on this machine. Sign in again below.
desktopDoor.credCloudCheckingWhy: The mail engine has not answered about this account's session yet.
desktopDoor.credSealFailedNote: Your sign-in could not be saved on this {machine}. ohmail keeps the one it has and tries again, so you stay signed in.
desktopDoor.credReadyWhy: Sealed under this install's key — kept in this {machine}'s keychain and mirrored to a file beside the app's data — and working.
desktopDoor.credAbsentWhy: No mailbox password is stored on this {machine}, so nothing is being synced yet.
desktopDoor.credUnreadableWhy: Something is stored, and this install's key does not open it. Entering it again seals it afresh; no mail is affected.
desktopDoor.credForeignWhy: The stored password was set up for a different mail server than this install is now using, so it has not been sent to the server it is set to. Open the mailbox settings, confirm the server you want and enter its password; no mail is affected.
desktopDoor.credUnknownWhy: The mail engine did not say, which happens when it is newer than this window. Nothing is wrong.
desktopDoor.engineWhyStarting: The process that opens your mailbox is coming up. Nothing is being synced until it does.
desktopDoor.engineWhyStopped: The process that opens your mailbox is not running, so nothing is being synced.
desktopDoor.engineWhyFailed: The process that opens your mailbox stopped and did not come back.
desktopDoor.engineWhyNoKey: This {machine}'s keystore would not answer, so the stored password cannot be opened.
desktopDoor.engineWhyUnknown: The mail engine did not say what it is doing, which happens when it is newer than this window.
desktopDoor.engineFailed: Stopped and did not come back
desktopDoor.installSignInAgainWhy: Your hosted session has gone. Signing in happens in the mail engine on this machine.
desktopDoor.installSwitchWhy: Open a different mail server, or move between this {machine} and your hosted account. The copy of your mail from this one is frozen where it is rather than deleted, so coming back does not cost a full re-sync.
desktopDoor.installSignOutConfirmWhy: The copy of your mail already on this {machine} stays where it is. What is cleared is the login — the stored password, or the session for your hosted account — and which door this install came in by. Nothing is removed from your mail server.
desktopDoor.installSignOutWhy: Clears the login and forgets which mailbox this is. Your mail stays on this {machine} and on your server.
desktopDoor.installPasswordNote: Your mailbox password goes from this window straight to the mail engine on this computer, which seals it under this install's key. It is never written to the app's settings file, and it never reaches us. A hosted account's session is not typed at all: the engine establishes that itself, and this window never holds it.
desktopDoor.mailtoIsDefaultWhy: Email links on this computer open a new message in ohmail.
desktopDoor.mailtoWhy: Which app opens email links (mailto) on this computer.
desktopDoor.mailtoAskBody: Clicking an email address anywhere on this computer would start a new message here. You can change this later in Settings.
desktopDoor.mailtoAfterDialog: macOS is applying the change — confirm its dialog if one appears.
desktopDoor.mailtoAfterSettings: Windows Settings is open — choose ohmail under Default apps.
desktopDoor.mailtoAfterSet: Mail links on this computer open in ohmail now.
desktopDoor.mailtoAfterPending: The change was sent to your desktop, and it has not taken effect yet.
desktopDoor.gateFoot: Your mail is untouched. It is on your own server, or in your hosted account, and this app has not changed either.
desktopDoor.gateKeyringTitle: This computer's keyring is not available
desktopDoor.gateKeyringWhy: ohmail keeps the key that protects your mailbox passwords in your login keyring, and the keyring did not answer: it is locked, or this computer has none. Unlock it, or create a login keyring (in GNOME with Passwords and Keys, in KDE with KWallet), then press Try again.
desktopDoor.gateKeychainWhy: ohmail keeps the key that protects your mailbox passwords in your login keychain, and the keychain did not answer. Unlock the login keychain in Keychain Access, then press Try again.
desktopDoor.gateCredentialsWhy: ohmail keeps the key that protects your mailbox passwords in Windows Credential Manager, and it did not answer. Press Try again; if it keeps happening, ohmail's log file has the details.
desktopDoor.gateLockedStore: Another copy of ohmail may still be running on this computer, or the app did not close cleanly last time. ohmail can remove the leftover lock and try again, but never while another copy is using it.
desktopDoor.gateUnlockRefused: The lock was kept: the program holding it is still running, most likely another copy of ohmail. Wait a moment and press again; if it keeps happening, restart this computer.
desktopDoor.gateUnlockNoEngine: Nothing was removed: ohmail could not get the mail engine ready to start. Press again in a moment; if it keeps happening, ohmail's log file has the details.
desktopDoor.gateUnlockNoAnswer: ohmail did not answer in time. If this card is still here in a moment, press again.
desktopDoor.gateEngineReported: The mail engine could not start ({name}). Quit ohmail and open it again; if it keeps happening, ohmail's log file has the details.
desktopDoor.gateStoreUnopenable: The copy of your mail on this computer could not be opened. Start over sets it aside and makes a new one from your mail; you may be asked for your mailbox password again.
desktopDoor.gateStartOverRefused: The copy could not be set aside, so nothing was changed. ohmail's log file has the details.
desktopDoor.gateRetryRefused: The mail engine could not be started again, so nothing changed. ohmail's log file has the details.
desktopDoor.gateKeyringStillLocked: Still not available, so nothing changed.
desktopDoor.accessLockSignOutRefused: Signing out did not finish ({reason}). Press Sign out to try again.
desktopDoor.gateSessionGone: You were signed out of your hosted account, so this install stopped receiving new mail. What was already here is kept; sign in again to reconnect.
desktopDoor.bootCreatingStore: Setting up your local mail store…
desktopDoor.bootMigratingOf: Updating your local mail store… ({applied} of {total})
desktopDoor.bootMigratingSlow: This can take several minutes on a large mailbox.
desktopDoor.bootCompacting: Compacting your local mail store — one-time maintenance…
desktopDoor.errorUnknown: Something went wrong and said nothing about what.
desktopDoor.doorHostSay: ohmail on another computer of yours organizes; this {machine} works through it. While that computer is off, this one shows its copy and can change nothing.
desktopDoor.doorHostUnavailable: Pairing with another computer isn't available in this version yet.
desktopDoor.hostAskLead: Paste the pairing link from ohmail on that computer — Settings → Devices → Add a device. Only the desktop app gives one out; the phone app cannot.
desktopDoor.hostLinkHint: It works once and expires five minutes after it was made.
desktopDoor.hostReachedLanAfter: — the same characters as under Settings → Devices there.
desktopDoor.hostReachedTs: Over your Tailscale, with a certificate this {machine} could verify.
desktopDoor.hostPairLead: Pairing adds this {machine} to that computer's Devices list, where it can be removed at any time. Your mail then comes from that computer and a copy is kept here.
desktopDoor.hostLinkShape: That is not a pairing link. It looks like https://…/pair#… and comes from Settings → Devices on that computer.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseCleartext: That link is a plain, unencrypted address, and ohmail will not send your mail over one. A computer running ohmail gives out a secure link — take it from Settings → Devices there.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseNoPin: That link does not carry that computer's key, so ohmail cannot tell its connection apart from anything else on your network. Make a new link from its Settings → Devices.
desktopDoor.hostRefusePinChanged: That computer's key has changed since this link was made, so ohmail stopped rather than trusting it. If ohmail was reinstalled there or restored from a backup, make a new link from its Settings → Devices. If not, something on your network is answering for it.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseNotOhmail: Something answered at {host}, but it is not ohmail. Check the link came from Settings → Devices on that computer.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseNotServing: ohmail is running on {host}, and it has not been set up to let your other devices use it. Turn that on there, under Settings → Devices, and make a new link.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseManaged: That link is from ohmail Cloud, not from a computer of yours. Go back and choose “ohmail Cloud”.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseServer: {host} is a server you run, not a computer sharing its mail. Go back and choose “Your own server”.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseAccountMismatch: This computer holds mail from a different account on {host} — it looks like ohmail was reinstalled there. Starting over discards the mail held here for that other account and reads {host}'s mailbox fresh. Your mail on the server is not touched. You will need a new pairing link, because the one you just used has been spent.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseRestartFirst: Nothing was paired. This computer is still finishing an earlier start over — quit ohmail and open it again, then pair with {host}. Your pairing link has not been used, so it will still work.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseSpent: That link is spent or expired. Make a new one from Settings → Devices on that computer.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseLinkUsed: That link was used before, so nothing was changed here. Make a new one from Settings → Devices on that computer.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseLinkExpired: That link has expired, so nothing was changed here. Make a new one from Settings → Devices on that computer.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseLinkRevoked: That link was taken back on that computer, so nothing was changed here. Make a new one from its Settings → Devices.
desktopDoor.hostRefusePairingUndone: The pairing was stopped here before {host} answered, so nothing was changed here.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseNotAnswering: {host} answered, but not the way ohmail does. Check the link came from Settings → Devices on that computer.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseNotSetUp: ohmail on {host} has not been set up yet. Finish setting it up there, then make a new link.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseNothingListening: Nothing is answering at {host}. Check that ohmail is open on that computer, then try again.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseTimedOut: {host} did not answer in time. Check that it is on, awake and on the same network as this computer.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseCertName: {host} answered with a certificate for a different name, so ohmail stopped. Make a new link from Settings → Devices on that computer.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseCertDate: {host} answered with a certificate that is not valid right now. Check the date and time on both computers.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseCertTrust: {host} answered with a certificate this computer does not trust, so ohmail stopped. Make a new link from Settings → Devices on that computer.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseUnknownName: This network does not know the name {host}. Check the link, and that both computers are on the same network.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseNoIdentity: Something answered at {host}, but it did not show an identity ohmail can check. Check the link came from Settings → Devices on that computer.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseRefused: {host} refused this pairing. Make a new link from Settings → Devices there and try again.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseRateLimited: Too many pairing attempts reached {host} from here. Wait a few minutes, then try again.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseAccountUnnamed: {host} did not say which account this pairing belongs to, and this computer already holds mail for one. Update ohmail on {host}, then pair again.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseSignedIn: This computer is already signed in, so nothing was paired. Sign out first, then pair again.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseIdentityPending: This computer is waiting for a browser confirmation for ohmail Cloud, so nothing was paired. Finish or cancel that first, then pair again.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseUnsupportedPlatform: This build of ohmail cannot tell {host} what kind of computer this is, and pairing without that would list it there as a browser. Nothing was paired.
desktopDoor.hostRefuseNoSession: {host} accepted the link and sent back no session, so nothing was paired. Make a new link from Settings → Devices there and try again.
desktopDoor.hostFootStaleWhy: Last answered {when}. This {machine} shows the copy it holds; nothing can be changed until that computer is back. If it will not be:
desktopDoor.hostCheckLan: Check that computer is on and that this {machine} is on the same network.
desktopDoor.hostCheckTs: Check that computer is on and signed in to your Tailscale.
desktopDoor.gateUnpaired: This {machine} is no longer paired with {host}. Pair again from its Settings → Devices, or set this {machine} up on its own. The copy of your mail here is kept.
desktopDoor.gateUnpairedRemoved: This {machine} is no longer paired with {host}. Pair again from its Settings → Devices, or set this {machine} up on its own. The copy of your mail here was removed.
desktopDoor.gateRestart: This computer is now paired with {host}. Quit ohmail and open it again to finish connecting — the copy of the mail that was here before is replaced on the next start.
desktopDoor.gateAccountErased: The ohmail account this {machine} was signed in to was deleted, so nothing new arrives here. Set this {machine} up on its own to keep reading your mail from your own server.
desktopDoor.mailboxWhyViaHost: The mailbox this {machine} reads through {host}, which organizes it.
desktopDoor.doorHostWhyLan: ohmail on {host} organizes; this {machine} reads and acts through it, over your network.
desktopDoor.doorHostWhyTs: ohmail on {host} organizes; this {machine} reads and acts through it, over your Tailscale ({origin}).
desktopDoor.credHostLiveWhy: This {machine} is on {host}'s Devices list. Removing it there ends the pairing.
desktopDoor.credHostOutWhy: The pairing with {host} has ended. Pair again below, or set this {machine} up on its own.
desktopDoor.credHostCheckingWhy: The mail engine has not answered about the pairing yet.
desktopDoor.connStaleWhy: Last answered {when}. This {machine} shows the copy it holds; nothing can be changed until that computer is back.
desktopDoor.installPairAgainWhy: The pairing with {host} has ended. A new link from its Settings → Devices pairs this {machine} again; the copy here is kept.
desktopDoor.takeoverLabel: Set this {machine} up on its own
desktopDoor.takeoverWhy: If {host} will not come back. This {machine} then opens your mail server itself and takes over the organizing. The copy from {host} is discarded and read again from the server; the mailboxes {host} held are listed first.
desktopDoor.takeoverLead: This {machine} will open your mail server itself and organize it, as {host} did. The copy from {host} is discarded and read again from the server. Nothing on the server changes until you agree to organize, one mailbox at a time.
desktopDoor.takeoverRest: {count, plural, one {The other mailbox: add it afterwards under Settings → Mailboxes.} other {The other # mailboxes: add them afterwards under Settings → Mailboxes.}}
desktopDoor.takeoverRosterUnknown: Could not read which mailboxes {host} held; enter the server by hand.
desktopDoor.installSwitchWhyHost: Open a different door: your own mail server, another computer, or a hosted account. The copy from {host} on this {machine} is discarded; your mailbox itself is untouched.
desktopDoor.pairingLeftAt: A pairing with {host} did not finish. This {machine} may still be listed on {host} under Settings → Devices.
desktopDoor.signedOutStillListed: Signed out on this {machine}. It may still be listed under Settings → Devices on {where} until it is removed there.
desktopDoor.changesWaiting: {count, plural, one {One change} other {# changes}} for {who} waiting on this {machine}. Sent when {who} signs in again here.
desktopDoor.installSignOutWhyHost: Ends the pairing with {host} and forgets which mailbox this is. Your mail stays on this {machine} and on your server.
desktopDoor.installSignOutConfirmWhyHost: The copy of your mail already on this {machine} stays where it is. What is cleared is the pairing with {host} and which door this install came in by. Nothing is removed from your mail server.
desktopDoor.aboutDoorHostWhy: ohmail on {host} opens your mailbox and organizes it; this {machine} reads and acts through it. Nothing about your mail is sent to us.
